title: Inside Samode Palace: The Royal Jaipur Venue Where Sharmiela Mandre Tied the Knot
excerpt: The 475-year-old heritage property in Rajasthan, where Mandre married producer Sudhan Sundaram, offers Mughal gardens, mirror-work halls, and full palace buyouts starting at ₹90 lakh
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Sharmiela Mandre married Sudhan Sundaram on July 12, 2026, at Samode Palace, Jaipur.
  • Samode Palace is a 475-year-old heritage property featuring Indo-Saracenic architecture and multiple wedding venues.
  • A full palace buyout for 90 guests costs approximately ₹90 lakh, plus additional event service fees.
  • Samode Bagh, a nearby Mughal-style garden, offers luxury accommodations for up to 300 guests.

  • Kannada actress Sharmiela Mandre married Tamil film producer Sudhan Sundaram on July 12, 2026, at Samode Palace in Jaipur, following South Indian Vedic rituals blended with Rajasthani traditions.
  • Samode Palace is a 475-year-old heritage property 43 kilometres northwest of Jaipur, featuring Indo-Saracenic architecture, a famed Sheesh Mahal (Hall of Mirrors), and multiple indoor and outdoor wedding venues.
  • The sister property Samode Bagh, a 20-acre Mughal-style garden seven minutes from the palace, offers 44 luxury tents and 27 garden suites — the oldest functioning Mughal garden in Rajasthan.
  • A full palace buyout for a two-night wedding accommodating 90 guests costs approximately ₹90 lakh plus taxes, positioning it as a premium but intimate destination wedding choice.

When Kannada actress and entrepreneur Sharmiela Mandre chose Samode Palace in Jaipur for her wedding to Tamil film producer Sudhan Sundaram on July 12, she joined a long line of couples drawn to one of Rajasthan's most storied heritage venues. The intimate ceremony, conducted according to South Indian Vedic rituals and followed by a grand reception, has drawn fresh attention to the 475-year-old property that sits at the foot of the Aravalli hills.

A Palace With Five Centuries of History

Samode Palace was originally built in the 16th century as a Rajput fort by Rawal Berisal, a high-ranking noble of the Amber and Jaipur principality. In the early 19th century, it was redesigned into the Indo-Saracenic masterpiece that stands today, blending Mughal and Rajasthani architectural traditions. The Samode family has maintained the property for over four centuries, converting it into a heritage hotel in 1987.

The palace houses 43 rooms and suites, including four royal suites with private courtyards, Jacuzzis, and fireplaces. Its standout feature is the Sheesh Mahal — a Hall of Mirrors adorned with intricately ornamented pillars, inlaid semi-precious stones, and vivid floral wall paintings that have been meticulously restored using traditional techniques.

The Wedding Venues

Samode Palace offers multiple event spaces: the Char Bagh outdoor lawn seats 200 guests for ceremonies, a rooftop terrace overlooking the palace accommodates 120, and intimate courtyards hold 60 to 80 guests for smaller rituals like Mehendi and Haldi. The Durbar Hall and Sultan Mahal serve as grand indoor venues for formal dinners and pre-wedding functions.

For larger celebrations, the palace partners with Samode Bagh, its sister property located just seven minutes away. Built by Rawal Sheo Singh, the Bagh is a 20-acre Mughal-style garden enclosed by 15-foot stone walls, featuring rows of fountains, pomegranate and citrus groves, and water channels fed by wells and captured rainwater. It is considered the oldest functional Mughal garden in Rajasthan.

Samode Bagh offers 44 luxury tents with air conditioning and modern amenities alongside 27 garden suites, collectively accommodating up to 300 additional guests. The property's dining area — a grand communal tent — serves Rajasthani, Asian, and European cuisine with options for poolside dining and open-air barbecues.

What It Costs

A full palace buyout for two nights and three days, with exclusive access to all venues and meals for up to 90 guests, starts at approximately ₹90 lakh (roughly $107,000) plus taxes. Event services — decoration, entertainment, photography, and styling — typically add ₹50 lakh or more depending on customization. Per-plate catering at Samode Bagh starts at ₹3,000 for vegetarian and ₹3,300 to ₹3,500 for non-vegetarian menus.

The Mandre-Sundaram Celebration

Mandre, known for her roles in films such as Krishna, Gaalipata 2, and Mirattal, and Sundaram, who runs Passion Studios and produced the National Award-winning film Parking and the Vijay Sethupathi starrer Maharaja, got engaged on June 25, 2026. Their two-day celebration began July 11 with traditional Haldi, Mehendi, and Sangeet ceremonies that blended Rajasthani and South Indian customs.

Director Atlee and actor Vijay Sethupathi were among the film industry guests expected at the celebration. The property, located 43 kilometres from Jaipur and 234 kilometres from Delhi, is accessible by road, rail, and air — a practical advantage for destination weddings drawing guests from multiple cities.

For Indian diaspora families considering heritage destination weddings in India, Samode Palace represents a category of venue that combines architectural authenticity with modern luxury — a formula that continues to attract couples from the film industry and beyond.
